title: What the charity registry filings add to existing cases
question: Do the renewal reports, audits, returns and letters filed with the Attorney General settle or change any figure in the existing cases?
finding: St. James Infirmary's books, filed with the registry for its dissolution, give the missing money an account name: $5.7 million booked as "Payments to Affiliates" in its last year, against $2.0 million of government contracts; the books also show $204,327 of liabilities, so its equity was $233.26, not $204,560. The Chinese Progressive Association owed Resilient Strategies $4.2 million at the end of 2022 and reports Resilient's Oakland suite as its own address. Mid Market Foundation reported $7,500.00 of revenue and $732.00 of assets for 2020; in fiscal 2022 the City paid it $12.2 million. United Council of Human Services lost its registration in September 2023.
how: Each figure is read with a fixed pattern from the named file (text layer or OCR) and the script stops if a pattern is not found. City payments come from the voucher file.
limits: "Payments to Affiliates" is an account name in a bookkeeping export, not an audited figure; it may record the write-off of the receivable as much as cash leaving, and the account does not name the affiliates (the dissolution request separately names five organizations to receive the remaining assets; that is not the same as saying where the booked payments went). Text read from scans can misplace digits; each figure should be checked against the image before it is quoted. A charity's delinquency with the State does not by itself bear on the services the City bought.

rows.label: Payments to affiliates, July 2023 to June 2024
rows.text: The profit-and-loss statement filed with the registry for the dissolution books $5,749,549.36 as "Payments to Affiliates" (account 80200), producing a net loss of $5,706,387.45; the tax return showed a small surplus and no such line.

rows.label: Liabilities at 30 June 2024
rows.text: The balance sheet shows total assets of $204,560.01 against liabilities of $204,326.75 (IRS taxes $70,000.00, an EIDL loan $123,591.75), leaving equity of $233.26. The $204,560 the case calls net assets is total assets.

rows.label: Government contracts in its last year
rows.text: Agency (government) contracts: $2,034,787.35 in the year to June 2024 (the City paid it $2,868,481.87 in fiscal 2024 by the voucher file). It also booked $70,000.00 of "IRS Taxes (Penalties & Fees)".

rows.label: Dissolution waivers
rows.text: The Attorney General waived objection to the disposition of its assets on 2025-01-14 and again on 2026-07-13; the organization wrote that it first asked in March 2024. The waiver asks for a final financial report once assets reach zero; none is on disk.

rows.label: Owed to Resilient Strategies, 31 Dec 2022
rows.text: The 2022 audit shows $4,216,807.00 payable to Resilient Strategies and $363,019.00 due from it, plus $4,508,381.00 payable to and $1,066,241.00 due from CEP; managed services cost $6,827,351.00 and a separate "administrative fee" $2,103,552.00. By the end of 2022 all employees but one had been moved to Resilient as employer of record.

rows.label: Owed to Resilient Strategies, 31 Dec 2021
rows.text: In its first year with Resilient (2021) the audit already shows $1,146,114.00 due to it.

rows.label: Address and contact on its registry reports
rows.text: Its amended 2022 renewal report (and the 2023 and 2024 reports) give 1212 Broadway Suite 700, Oakland, the principal office of Resilient Strategies, and a resilientstrategiesllc.com e-mail as the charity's own contact.

rows.label: Gross revenue, 2020
rows.text: Its 2020 renewal report gives gross revenue of $7,500.00 and total assets of $732.00, with a Novato address; the City paid it $12,165,000.00 in fiscal 2022 by the voucher file, the first year of its grant (contract 1000026131 in the existing case). The registry now shows it past due.

rows.label: Registration revoked
rows.text: The registry revoked its registration on 09/18/2023 after more than a year of suspension, for renewal reports not filed for fiscal years ending 12/31/2021, 12/31/2022, and 12/31/2023; the letter also says its 2018 report claimed no audit when one was required. A revoked charity may not spend charitable assets without the Attorney General's approval.

rows.label: First delinquency notice
rows.text: The registry's first delinquency notice is dated 12 April 2024; the City paid the center $375,719.96 in fiscal 2023, its last year of payments.

rows.label: Explanation of negative net assets, 2024 report
rows.text: Its 2024 renewal report says the balance sheet "shows negative net assets" and that the repayment terms of a "large unsecured loan liability" were being renegotiated; it lists the Public Utilities Commission, economic-development office, City Administrator, children's department and Arts Commission among its government funders.

rows.label: 2022 return (newly on file)
rows.text: A 2022 return the case did not have: revenue $625,025.70, all of it government grants; expenses $556,484.50; "revenue less expenses" printed as $63,772.28 although the difference is $68,541.20; total assets 0 and net assets $50,000.00. The renewal report for 2022 also gives total assets of $0.00. Read from the scan's text layer.
